editorial.headline: Precision Machinery, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28140 covers the industrial making of bearings, gears, clutches and mechanical transmission components, with a clear national opening and a hard Bali stop for PMA registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28140 is a manufacturing code for the quiet hardware inside moving machines: ball and roller bearings, bearing rings and parts, gears, gearboxes, speed changers, clutches and clutch shafts, pulleys, linked chain elements, and power-transmission chains. It also reaches into the component layer of mechanical transmission equipment, including cam shafts, crank shafts, cranks, bearing frames, simple shaft bearings, bearing blocks, gear assemblies, clutches, pulleys and related mechanical drive parts. In plain English, this is not a general metalworking label. It is a code for businesses that make the parts that let industrial motion turn, carry, couple, reduce, transmit and repeat reliably.

That breadth matters because the record opens the activity across every stated business scale: micro, small, medium and large. A founder using this code is not merely describing trading or repair activity; the scope is anchored in production. The activity can fit a workshop making specific transmission parts, a more specialised component producer, or a larger factory manufacturing the bearing, gear and drive elements named in the scope. The common thread is mechanical transmission: parts that sit between power and movement, whether in the form of bearings, gears, shafts, chains, pulleys or coupling systems.

Nationally, the investment picture is straightforward. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, and the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. That means the national classification does not, in this slim record, impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The national position is grounded in Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup outside the Bali constraint, the code reads as nationally open, with the full stated scale range available and no lower foreign-ownership percentage appearing in the record.

Bali is the decisive exception. The record marks this activity as blocked in Bali for PMA registration, with the status Blocked (risk class). The reason given is not a separate Bali percentage, quota or partnership rule; it is a risk-class moratorium: OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, and Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. So the honest reading is simple: KBLI 28140 may be nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, but a foreigner cannot register this activity as a PMA in Bali today under the record supplied.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 28140 is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but the Bali record turns that opening into a hard local stop for PMA registration.
